requirements.title: Platform must satisfy administrative, physical and technical safeguards for PHI
requirements.description: Any system component that creates, receives, maintains or transmits Protected Health Information must implement the administrative, physical and technical safeguards set out in the regulatory brief.
requirements.quote: Any system that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI must satisfy the administrative, physical and technical safeguards below.

requirements.title: Compliance with HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E)
requirements.description: The platform's requirements derive from the HIPAA Privacy Rule as codified in 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E, and the platform must comply with it when handling PHI.
requirements.quote: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E)

requirements.title: Compliance with HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)
requirements.description: The platform must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule as codified in 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C.
requirements.quote: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)

requirements.title: Compliance with HITECH Act breach notification provisions
requirements.description: The platform must meet the breach notification provisions of the HITECH Act when PHI is compromised.
requirements.quote: HITECH Act breach notification provisions

requirements.title: Compliance with 42 CFR Part 2 for substance use disorder records
requirements.description: The platform must comply with 42 CFR Part 2 governing the confidentiality of substance use disorder patient records.
requirements.quote: 42 CFR Part 2 (substance use disorder records)

requirements.title: GDPR applies where the platform processes data for EU patients
requirements.description: GDPR requirements apply to the platform in cases where it processes personal data for patients located in the EU.
requirements.quote: GDPR, where the platform processes data for patients in the EU

requirements.title: Requirements scope covers covered entities and business associates
requirements.description: The platform handles Protected Health Information on behalf of covered entities and their business associates, so requirements must be met in both roles.
requirements.quote: This document sets out the regulatory requirements for a platform handling Protected Health Information (PHI) on behalf of covered entities and their business associates.

requirements.title: Minimum necessary limitation on PHI access
requirements.description: Access to PHI must be limited to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, covering uses, disclosures and requests.
requirements.quote: Access to PHI must be limited to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose. This applies to uses, disclosures and requests.

requirements.title: Role-based access control mapped to job function
requirements.description: The system must implement role-based access control in which roles are mapped to job function.
requirements.quote: Role-based access control, with roles mapped to job function

requirements.title: Record-level access decisions
requirements.description: Access decisions must be made at the record level rather than the system level, so that a user such as a scheduling clerk can see appointment times without seeing clinical notes.
requirements.quote: Record-level access decisions, not system-level: a scheduling clerk may see appointment times without seeing clinical notes

requirements.title: Break-glass access for emergency treatment
requirements.description: Break-glass access is permitted for emergency treatment, but every such access must be logged and reviewed.
requirements.quote: Break-glass access for emergency treatment, permitted but always logged and reviewed

requirements.title: Access reviews at least every 90 days
requirements.description: Access reviews must be conducted at least once every 90 days, and the results of those reviews must be retained.
requirements.quote: Access reviews at least every 90 days, with results retained

requirements.title: Out-of-role record retrieval requires a break-glass event record
requirements.description: No user may retrieve a record outside their assigned role unless a break-glass event is written.
requirements.quote: No user may retrieve a record outside their assigned role without a break-glass event being written

requirements.title: Privacy officer review of break-glass events within 5 business days
requirements.description: Every break-glass event must be reviewed by a privacy officer within 5 business days of occurring.
requirements.quote: Break-glass events must be reviewed by a privacy officer within 5 business days
requirements.trigger: A break-glass access event is logged

requirements.title: Access review completion evidence
requirements.description: Completion of an access review must be evidenced with the reviewer's identity and the date of review.
requirements.quote: Access review completion is evidenced with reviewer identity and date

requirements.title: Patient request for copy of designated record set
requirements.description: The system must allow patients to request and receive a copy of their designated record set.
requirements.quote: Patients may request a copy of their designated record set
requirements.happyPath: Patient submits an access request, the covered entity locates the designated record set and provides a copy

requirements.title: 30-day response deadline for access requests
requirements.description: A response to a patient access request must be issued within 30 calendar days of the request.
requirements.quote: Response required within 30 calendar days, with one 30-day extension permitted if the patient is notified in writing

requirements.title: Single 30-day extension requires written notice
requirements.description: One 30-day extension of the access response deadline is permitted only if the patient is notified in writing.
requirements.quote: Response required within 30 calendar days, with one 30-day extension permitted if the patient is notified in writing

requirements.title: Electronic copies in requested form and format
requirements.description: Where readily producible, electronic copies of records must be provided in the form and format the patient requested.
requirements.quote: Electronic copies must be provided in the form and format requested where readily producible

requirements.title: Access fees limited to reasonable cost-based charges
requirements.description: Fees charged for providing record copies are limited to reasonable, cost-based charges covering labour and media only.
requirements.quote: Fees limited to reasonable, cost-based charges for labour and media

requirements.title: Patient request to amend inaccurate records
requirements.description: Patients may submit a request to amend records they believe to be inaccurate.
requirements.quote: Patients may request amendment of records they believe inaccurate
requirements.trigger: Patient believes a record is inaccurate and submits an amendment request
requirements.happyPath: Patient submits an amendment request, the covered entity reviews it and acts within the required timeframe

requirements.title: 60-day deadline to act on amendment requests
requirements.description: The covered entity must act on a request to amend records within 60 days, with one permitted 30-day extension.
requirements.quote: The covered entity must act within 60 days, with one 30-day extension

requirements.title: Amendment denial must state basis and disagreement right
requirements.description: A denial of an amendment request must state the basis for denial and inform the patient of the right to submit a statement of disagreement.
requirements.quote: Denials must state the basis and the patient's right to submit a statement of disagreement

requirements.title: Amendments and disagreements follow the record on disclosure
requirements.description: Amendments and statements of disagreement must be included with the record wherever that record is disclosed.
requirements.quote: Amendments and disagreements must travel with the record wherever it is disclosed

requirements.title: Accounting of disclosures covers six years prior to request
requirements.description: Patients may request an accounting of disclosures covering the six-year period immediately before the request.
requirements.quote: Patients may request an accounting of disclosures for the six years prior to the request

requirements.title: Required content of the disclosure accounting
requirements.description: Each entry in the accounting of disclosures must include the date, the recipient, a description of the PHI disclosed, and the purpose of the disclosure.
requirements.quote: The accounting must include date, recipient, description of PHI disclosed, and purpose

requirements.title: Treatment, payment and operations disclosures excluded
requirements.description: Disclosures made for treatment, payment and healthcare operations are not included in the accounting of disclosures.
requirements.quote: Disclosures for treatment, payment and operations are excluded from the accounting

requirements.title: One free accounting per 12 months
requirements.description: The covered entity must provide one accounting of disclosures free of charge in any 12-month period.
requirements.quote: One accounting per 12 months must be provided free of charge

requirements.title: Unique user identification for PHI system access
requirements.description: Every individual granted access to systems containing PHI must be assigned a unique user identifier, so that activity can be attributed to a single named person.
requirements.quote: Unique user identification for every individual with access

requirements.title: Automatic logoff after inactivity
requirements.description: Sessions in systems containing PHI must terminate automatically once a defined period of inactivity has elapsed.
requirements.quote: Automatic logoff after a period of inactivity

requirements.title: Encryption of PHI is addressable, with justification required if absent
requirements.description: Encryption and decryption of PHI is an addressable safeguard; where encryption is not implemented, the absence must be documented and a justification recorded.
requirements.quote: Encryption and decryption of PHI (addressable, but the absence of encryption must be documented and justified)

requirements.title: Audit mechanisms recording activity in PHI systems
requirements.description: The organisation must implement hardware, software or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use PHI.
requirements.quote: Hardware, software or procedural mechanisms recording activity in systems containing PHI

requirements.title: Required audit record fields
requirements.description: Each audit record must capture user identity, timestamp, record accessed, action taken, and the outcome of the action.
requirements.quote: Audit records must capture: user identity, timestamp, record accessed, action taken, and outcome

requirements.title: Audit logs retained for six years
requirements.description: Audit logs must be kept for a retention period of six years.
requirements.quote: Audit logs must be retained for six years and protected from alteration

requirements.title: Audit logs protected from alteration
requirements.description: Audit logs must be protected against alteration so that recorded activity cannot be modified after the fact.
requirements.quote: Audit logs must be retained for six years and protected from alteration

requirements.title: Integrity authentication for PHI
requirements.description: Mechanisms must be in place to authenticate that PHI has not been improperly altered or destroyed.
requirements.quote: Mechanisms to authenticate that PHI has not been improperly altered or destroyed

requirements.title: Version history for clinical records
requirements.description: Clinical records must maintain a version history in which prior values are retrievable.
requirements.quote: Version history for clinical records, with prior values retrievable

requirements.title: Encryption in transit for PHI leaving the network
requirements.description: All PHI leaving the organisation's network must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 as a minimum.
requirements.quote: Encryption in transit for all PHI leaving the organisation's network (TLS 1.2 minimum)

requirements.title: Integrity controls detect modification in transit
requirements.description: Transmission security must include integrity controls capable of detecting modification of data while in transit.
requirements.quote: Integrity controls to detect modification in transit

requirements.title: Encryption at rest must use AES-256
requirements.description: Data at rest must be encrypted using the AES-256 standard.
requirements.quote: At rest: AES-256

requirements.title: Encryption in transit must use TLS 1.2 or higher
requirements.description: Data in transit must be protected using TLS version 1.2 or higher.
requirements.quote: In transit: TLS 1.2 or higher

requirements.title: Key management separated from data storage with documented rotation
requirements.description: Encryption key management must be kept separate from the data storage it protects, and key rotation must be documented.
requirements.quote: Key management separated from data storage, with documented rotation

requirements.title: Impermissible use or disclosure presumed a breach
requirements.description: Any impermissible use or disclosure of PHI must be treated as a breach by default. The presumption can only be rebutted where a documented risk assessment demonstrates a low probability that the PHI has been compromised.
requirements.quote: An impermissible use or disclosure of PHI is presumed a breach unless a risk assessment demonstrates a low probability that the PHI has been compromised.

requirements.title: Four-factor breach risk assessment
requirements.description: The breach risk assessment must evaluate: the nature and extent of the PHI involved including identifiers and likelihood of re-identification; the unauthorised person who used or received the PHI; whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed; and the extent to which the risk has been mitigated.
requirements.quote: Nature and extent of the PHI involved, including identifiers and likelihood of re-identification

requirements.title: Assess whether PHI was actually acquired or viewed
requirements.description: The risk assessment must determine whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed by the unauthorised recipient, and the extent to which the risk has since been mitigated.
requirements.quote: Whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed

requirements.title: Notify affected individuals within 60 calendar days of discovery
requirements.description: Affected individuals must be notified without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days from the date the breach was discovered.
requirements.quote: Affected individuals: without unreasonable delay, and no later than 60 calendar days from discovery

requirements.title: Notify HHS within 60 days for breaches affecting 500 or more individuals
requirements.description: Breaches affecting 500 or more individuals must be reported to the Department of Health and Human Services within 60 days of discovery.
requirements.quote: Department of Health and Human Services: within 60 days for breaches affecting 500 or more individuals; annually for smaller breaches

requirements.title: Annual HHS reporting for breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals
requirements.description: Breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals are reported to the Department of Health and Human Services on an annual basis rather than within the 60-day window.
requirements.quote: annually for smaller breaches

requirements.title: Media notice for breaches affecting more than 500 state residents
requirements.description: Where a breach affects more than 500 residents of a single state or jurisdiction, notice to prominent media serving that state or jurisdiction is required.
requirements.quote: Media notice: required for breaches affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction

requirements.title: Business associate must notify covered entity within 60 days
requirements.description: A business associate that discovers a breach must notify the covered entity within 60 days of discovery so the covered entity can meet its own notification obligations.
requirements.quote: Business associates must notify the covered entity within 60 days of discovery

requirements.title: Required content of a breach notification
requirements.description: Every breach notification must include a description of what happened with the date of the breach and its discovery, the types of information involved, steps individuals should take to protect themselves, what the entity is doing to investigate and mitigate, and contact procedures.
requirements.quote: Description of what happened and the date of the breach and its discovery

requirements.title: Notification must state protective steps and mitigation activity
requirements.description: The notification content must tell individuals what steps to take to protect themselves, describe the entity's investigation and mitigation activity, and give contact procedures for further enquiries.
requirements.quote: Steps individuals should take to protect themselves

requirements.title: Written BAA required before business associate PHI access
requirements.description: A written business associate agreement must be executed before any business associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on behalf of the covered entity.
requirements.quote: A written agreement is required before a business associate may create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on the covered entity's behalf.

requirements.title: BAA must limit permitted uses and disclosures
requirements.description: The agreement must specify permitted uses and disclosures of PHI, which may be no broader than the covered entity's own permitted uses and disclosures.
requirements.quote: Permitted uses and disclosures, no broader than the covered entity's own

requirements.title: BAA must obligate Security Rule safeguards
requirements.description: The agreement must include the business associate's obligation to implement Security Rule safeguards.
requirements.quote: Obligation to implement Security Rule safeguards

requirements.title: BAA must require reporting of security incidents and breaches
requirements.description: The agreement must obligate the business associate to report security incidents and breaches.
requirements.quote: Obligation to report security incidents and breaches

requirements.title: Subcontractor flow-down of BAA terms
requirements.description: The same agreement terms must bind any subcontractor of the business associate.
requirements.quote: Subcontractor flow-down: the same terms must bind any subcontractor

requirements.title: Return or destruction of PHI at termination
requirements.description: The agreement must require return or destruction of PHI at termination of the agreement, where feasible.
requirements.quote: Return or destruction of PHI at termination where feasible

requirements.title: Six-year retention of HIPAA documentation
requirements.description: HIPAA documentation, including policies, authorisations and agreements, must be retained for six years from creation or from the last effective date, whichever is later.
requirements.quote: HIPAA documentation (policies, authorisations, agreements) retained six years from creation or last effective date

requirements.title: Longer state medical record retention period governs
requirements.description: Where a state medical record retention period differs from and exceeds the six-year HIPAA period, the longer period applies to the record.
requirements.quote: State medical record retention periods vary and may exceed six years; the longer period governs

requirements.title: Audit logs retained six years
requirements.description: Audit logs must be retained for six years.
requirements.quote: Audit logs retained six years

requirements.title: Media sanitisation before disposal or reuse
requirements.description: Storage media must be sanitised before it is disposed of or reused, to prevent recovery of the data it held.
requirements.quote: Media sanitisation before disposal or reuse

requirements.title: Certificates of destruction retained for third-party disposal
requirements.description: When disposal is performed by a third party, certificates of destruction must be obtained and retained as evidence.
requirements.quote: Certificates of destruction retained for third-party disposal

requirements.title: Consent required for disclosure of substance use disorder records
requirements.description: Substance use disorder records governed by 42 CFR Part 2 are held to a stricter standard than HIPAA: patient consent must be obtained for most disclosures, including disclosures made for treatment purposes.
requirements.quote: Stricter than HIPAA: consent required for most disclosures, including for treatment

requirements.title: Redisclosure of Part 2 records prohibited without further consent
requirements.description: Once substance use disorder records have been disclosed, the recipient may not redisclose them unless further patient consent is obtained.
requirements.quote: Redisclosure prohibited without further consent

requirements.title: Substance use disorder records segregable from general medical record
requirements.description: The system must keep substance use disorder records separable from the general medical record so that Part 2 protected data can be identified and handled distinctly.
requirements.quote: Records must be segregable from the general medical record

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes excluded from right of access
requirements.description: Psychotherapy notes are not subject to the patient right of access and must be withheld from access request fulfilment.
requirements.quote: Excluded from the right of access

requirements.title: Specific separate authorisation required for psychotherapy note disclosure
requirements.description: Most disclosures of psychotherapy notes require a specific authorisation that is separate and distinct from a general consent.
requirements.quote: Require specific authorisation for most disclosures, separate from a general consent

requirements.title: Access provisioning completed before first login
requirements.description: User access must be provisioned by identity administration before the user's first login, with an audit trail recording the role granted and the approver.
requirements.quote: | Access provisioning | Before first login | Identity administration | Yes — role and approver |

requirements.title: Break-glass access reviewed within 5 business days
requirements.description: The privacy officer must review each break-glass access event within 5 business days, and the audit trail must capture the reviewer and the outcome of the review.
requirements.quote: | Break-glass review | Within 5 business days | Privacy officer | Yes — reviewer and outcome |

requirements.title: Right of access response within 30 days with one extension
requirements.description: Health information management must respond to an individual's right of access request within 30 days, with a maximum of one extension permitted. The request and its fulfilment must be recorded in an audit trail.
requirements.quote: | Right of access response | 30 days, one extension | Health information management | Yes — request and fulfilment |

requirements.title: Amendment decision within 60 days with one extension
requirements.description: Health information management must decide on a record amendment request within 60 days, with one extension permitted. The decision and the basis for it must be captured in an audit trail.
requirements.quote: | Amendment decision | 60 days, one extension | Health information management | Yes — decision and basis |

requirements.title: Breach risk assessment performed on discovery
requirements.description: The privacy officer must perform a breach risk assessment upon discovery of a potential breach, documenting all four assessment factors in the audit trail.
requirements.quote: | Breach risk assessment | On discovery | Privacy officer | Yes — four factors documented |

requirements.title: Individual breach notification within 60 days of discovery
requirements.description: The privacy officer must notify affected individuals within 60 days from discovery of the breach, recording the notification date and method in the audit trail.
requirements.quote: | Individual notification | 60 days from discovery | Privacy officer | Yes — date and method |

requirements.title: HHS notification within 60 days for breaches affecting 500 or more
requirements.description: Compliance must notify HHS within 60 days for breaches affecting 500 or more individuals, retaining the submission receipt as the audit trail.
requirements.quote: | HHS notification | 60 days (500+) or annual | Compliance | Yes — submission receipt |

requirements.title: Annual HHS notification for smaller breaches
requirements.description: Breaches below the 500-individual threshold are reported to HHS on an annual basis by Compliance, with the submission receipt retained as evidence.
requirements.quote: | HHS notification | 60 days (500+) or annual | Compliance | Yes — submission receipt |

requirements.title: Access review every 90 days by system owner
requirements.description: The system owner must review user access at least every 90 days, with the reviewer identity and review date captured in an audit trail.
requirements.quote: | Access review | Every 90 days | System owner | Yes — reviewer and date |

requirements.title: Audit logs retained for 6 years
requirements.description: Platform operations must retain audit logs for 6 years, evidenced by a documented retention policy.
requirements.quote: | Audit log retention | 6 years | Platform operations | Yes — retention policy |

requirements.title: Audit trail required for every compliance obligation
requirements.description: Each compliance obligation in the summary requires a corresponding audit trail capturing the specified evidence elements (for example reviewer and date, decision and basis, submission receipt).
requirements.quote: | Requirement | Timing | Responsibility | Audit Trail Required |

requirements.title: Low risk tier definition
requirements.description: Data classified as Low risk consists of de-identified data and aggregate reporting where no re-identification key is held by the organization.
requirements.quote: **Low:** De-identified data, aggregate reporting, no re-identification key held

requirements.title: Moderate risk tier definition
requirements.description: Data classified as Moderate risk is a limited data set governed by a data use agreement, from which direct identifiers have been removed.
requirements.quote: **Moderate:** Limited data set under a data use agreement; direct identifiers removed

requirements.title: High risk tier definition
requirements.description: Data classified as High risk is full PHI including identifiers, accessed by clinical staff.
requirements.quote: **High:** Full PHI including identifiers, accessed by clinical staff

requirements.title: Critical risk tier definition
requirements.description: Data classified as Critical risk comprises substance use disorder records, psychotherapy notes, HIV information and genetic information.
requirements.quote: **Critical:** Substance use disorder records, psychotherapy notes, HIV and genetic information

requirements.title: Risk tier drives controls, monitoring and consent
requirements.description: The assigned risk tier must determine the applicable access controls, the frequency of monitoring and the consent requirements for the data.
requirements.quote: Risk tier determines access controls, monitoring frequency and consent requirements.

requirements.title: No PHI access without provisioned role or logged break-glass
requirements.description: PHI access must occur only through a provisioned role, or via a break-glass event that is logged; there must be no other access path.
requirements.quote: No access to PHI without a provisioned role or a logged break-glass event

requirements.title: Complete capture of PHI access events
requirements.description: 100% of PHI access events must be captured, each including the user, the timestamp and the record accessed.
requirements.quote: 100% of PHI access events captured with user, timestamp and record

requirements.title: Right-of-access fulfilment within 30 days, measured
requirements.description: Patient right-of-access requests must be fulfilled within 30 days, and fulfilment time must be measured.
requirements.quote: Right-of-access requests fulfilled within 30 days, measured

requirements.title: Breach risk assessments documented against all four factors
requirements.description: Every breach risk assessment must be documented and address all four required factors.
requirements.quote: Breach risk assessments documented against all four factors

requirements.title: Immutable audit logs retained six years
requirements.description: Audit logs must be immutable and retained for six years, and this must be demonstrable to an auditor.
requirements.quote: Audit logs immutable and retained six years, demonstrable to an auditor

requirements.title: Encryption at rest and in transit verified by configuration audit
requirements.description: Encryption must be in place both at rest and in transit, with verification performed through a configuration audit.
requirements.quote: Encryption at rest and in transit verified by configuration audit

requirements.title: Business associate agreements executed before PHI sharing
requirements.description: A business associate agreement must be in place before any PHI is shared with that party.
requirements.quote: Business associate agreements in place before any PHI is shared

requirements.title: MVP scope covers record access, consent, audit and disclosure
requirements.description: The initial release scope is limited to patient record access, consent management, audit, and disclosure handling.
requirements.quote: **Scope:** MVP — patient record access, consent management, audit and disclosure handling

requirements.title: Every record access must be accountable
requirements.description: The platform must provide clinicians with fast access to needed records while ensuring every access event is accountable (logged and attributable).
requirements.quote: Give clinicians fast access to the records they need while making every access accountable.

requirements.title: Record lookup time reduced from minutes to seconds
requirements.description: The platform must reduce the time required to locate a patient record from minutes to seconds.
requirements.quote: The platform must reduce the time to locate a patient record from minutes to seconds

requirements.title: Surface only access events warranting privacy-officer attention
requirements.description: The platform must reduce privacy-officer review effort by filtering and surfacing only those access events that warrant attention.
requirements.quote: reduce privacy-officer review effort by surfacing only the access events that warrant attention

requirements.title: Role-based access control governed by clinical role
requirements.description: Access to record sections must be governed by the user's clinical role so that staff can see only the data their job requires.
requirements.quote: As a privacy officer, I want access to be governed by clinical role so that staff see only what their job requires.

requirements.title: Defined set of clinical roles
requirements.description: The system supports six roles: attending clinician, nurse, scheduling clerk, billing analyst, privacy officer, and system administrator.
requirements.quote: Roles: attending clinician, nurse, scheduling clerk, billing analyst, privacy officer, system administrator

requirements.title: Role-to-record-section permission mapping
requirements.description: Each role maps to a permitted set of record sections: demographics, encounters, medications, clinical notes, psychotherapy notes, substance use records, and billing.
requirements.quote: Each role maps to a permitted set of record sections: demographics, encounters, medications, clinical notes, psychotherapy notes, substance use records, billing

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes and substance use records excluded by default
requirements.description: Psychotherapy notes and substance use records are excluded from every role by default and can only be reached through an explicit per-patient grant.
requirements.quote: Psychotherapy notes and substance use records are excluded from every role by default and require explicit per-patient grant

requirements.title: Two-person approval for role assignment
requirements.description: Role assignment requires approval by a second person, and the system rejects self-approval.
requirements.quote: Role assignment requires approval by a second person; self-approval is rejected by the system

requirements.title: Access reviews generated every 90 days
requirements.description: The system generates access reviews every 90 days listing every user and their effective permissions.
requirements.quote: Access reviews generated every 90 days, listing every user and their effective permissions

requirements.title: Out-of-scope access attempt denied and logged
requirements.description: A scheduling clerk attempting to retrieve a clinical note receives a permission error and the attempt is recorded in the log.
requirements.quote: A scheduling clerk retrieving a clinical note receives a permission error, and the attempt is logged

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes require per-patient authorisation record
requirements.description: No role may grant access to psychotherapy notes unless an explicit per-patient authorisation record exists.
requirements.quote: No role grants access to psychotherapy notes without an explicit per-patient authorisation record

requirements.title: Role changes propagate within 60 seconds with approver identity
requirements.description: Role changes take effect within 60 seconds and are recorded together with the identity of the approver.
requirements.quote: Role changes take effect within 60 seconds and are recorded with approver identity

requirements.title: Access review export contents
requirements.description: The access review export must include user, role, last login and records accessed in the period.
requirements.quote: Access review export includes user, role, last login and records accessed in the period

requirements.title: Emergency clinician break-glass access to an out-of-scope record
requirements.description: An emergency clinician facing a life-at-risk situation states a reason from a fixed list plus free text and is granted immediate access to a record outside their normal scope, with the event queued for privacy officer review and the patient notified.
requirements.quote: As an emergency clinician, I want to reach a record outside my normal scope when a patient's life is at risk, so that care is not delayed by a permission boundary.
requirements.trigger: A patient's life is at risk and the needed record is outside the clinician's normal access scope
requirements.happyPath: Clinician invokes break-glass, selects a reason from the fixed list and adds free text, access is granted immediately for up to 4 hours, the event is queued for privacy officer review, and the patient is notified within 30 days.

requirements.title: Break-glass reason capture
requirements.description: Break-glass access requires the user to state a reason chosen from a fixed list plus accompanying free text.
requirements.quote: Break-glass requires a stated reason from a fixed list plus free text

requirements.title: No approval step in break-glass path
requirements.description: Break-glass access is granted immediately with no approval required in the access path.
requirements.quote: Access granted immediately; no approval in the path

requirements.title: Break-glass session limited to 4 hours
requirements.description: A break-glass session is limited to 4 hours, after which re-authorisation is required.
requirements.quote: Session limited to 4 hours, then re-authorisation required

requirements.title: Break-glass events queued for privacy officer review
requirements.description: Every break-glass event is placed in a queue for review by the privacy officer.
requirements.quote: Every break-glass event queued for privacy officer review

requirements.title: Patient notification of break-glass access within 30 days
requirements.description: The patient must be notified of break-glass access to their record within 30 days.
requirements.quote: Patient notified of break-glass access to their record within 30 days

requirements.title: Break-glass access granted in under 5 seconds
requirements.description: Break-glass must grant access in under 5 seconds, since delay constitutes a clinical risk.
requirements.quote: Break-glass grants access in under 5 seconds — a delay here is a clinical risk

requirements.title: Break-glass event reaches review queue within 60 seconds
requirements.description: Every break-glass event must appear in the privacy officer queue within 60 seconds.
requirements.quote: Every event appears in the privacy officer queue within 60 seconds

requirements.title: No bulk dismissal of break-glass reviews
requirements.description: The review queue cannot be dismissed in bulk; each break-glass event requires an individual decision.
requirements.quote: Review queue cannot be dismissed in bulk; each event requires an individual decision

requirements.title: Break-glass audit trail contents
requirements.description: The break-glass audit trail must record user, patient, reason, records viewed, duration, reviewer and outcome.
requirements.quote: Audit trail: user, patient, reason, records viewed, duration, reviewer, outcome

requirements.title: Record consents and authorisations against the patient record
requirements.description: The system must capture consents and authorisations linked to the patient so that outbound disclosures can be validated automatically against the recorded permissions.
requirements.quote: I want consents and authorisations recorded against the patient so that disclosures can be checked against them automatically

requirements.title: Support the five defined consent types
requirements.description: The system must support consent capture for general treatment consent, research participation, marketing, substance use disorder disclosure (42 CFR Part 2), and psychotherapy notes authorisation.
requirements.quote: Consent types: general treatment consent, research participation, marketing, substance use disorder disclosure (42 CFR Part 2), psychotherapy notes authorisation

requirements.title: Mandatory consent attributes
requirements.description: Every consent record must capture scope, recipient class, purpose, effective date, expiry date, and method of capture.
requirements.quote: Each consent records: scope, recipient class, purpose, effective date, expiry date, and method of capture

requirements.title: Consents are revocable with immediate effect and timestamp
requirements.description: Consents must be revocable. A revocation takes effect immediately for all future disclosures and is recorded with a timestamp.
requirements.quote: Consents are revocable; revocation is effective immediately for future disclosures and recorded with a timestamp

requirements.title: Expired consent blocks disclosure but not treatment access
requirements.description: An expired consent must not prevent access to the record for treatment purposes, but must block the specific disclosure that the consent governed.
requirements.quote: Expired consents must not block treatment access, but must block the disclosure they governed

requirements.title: Disclosure without matching active consent is refused and logged
requirements.description: When a disclosure is attempted and no matching active consent exists, the system refuses the disclosure and writes a log entry for it.
requirements.quote: A disclosure attempt without a matching active consent is refused and logged

requirements.title: Revocation propagates to disclosure checks within 60 seconds
requirements.description: A consent revocation must be reflected in downstream disclosure checks no more than 60 seconds after it is recorded.
requirements.quote: Revocation propagates to disclosure checks within 60 seconds

requirements.title: Part 2 consent required for substance use disorder disclosure
requirements.description: Substance use disorder records must not be disclosed unless a specific 42 CFR Part 2 consent is in place; a general consent never satisfies this requirement.
requirements.quote: Substance use disorder records cannot be disclosed without a Part 2 consent, regardless of any general consent

requirements.title: Full consent history retained and revoked consents never deleted
requirements.description: The complete history of consents must be retained; a revoked consent is preserved rather than deleted from the record.
requirements.quote: Consent history is retained in full; a revoked consent is never deleted

requirements.title: Health information manager captures a patient consent
requirements.description: A health information manager records a consent or authorisation against a patient, entering its scope, recipient class, purpose, effective and expiry dates and capture method, so that subsequent disclosure requests are checked automatically against it.
requirements.quote: As a health information manager, I want consents and authorisations recorded against the patient so that disclosures can be checked against them automatically.
requirements.trigger: A patient provides a consent or authorisation that must be recorded
requirements.happyPath: The manager selects the consent type, records scope, recipient class, purpose, effective date, expiry date and method of capture, and the consent becomes available to automated disclosure checks.

requirements.title: Audit entry generated for every PHI access event
requirements.description: The system must generate an audit entry for every read, write, export and print action performed on PHI.
requirements.quote: Every read, write, export and print of PHI generates an audit entry

requirements.title: Required audit entry data fields
requirements.description: Each audit entry must record user identity, role at time of access, patient identifier, record section, action, timestamp, source IP, and outcome.
requirements.quote: Entry contains: user identity, role at time of access, patient identifier, record section, action, timestamp, source IP, and outcome

requirements.title: Append-only audit storage
requirements.description: Audit storage must be append-only, with no application path permitting update or delete of audit entries.
requirements.quote: Audit storage is append-only; no application path permits update or delete

requirements.title: Audit retention of six years minimum
requirements.description: Audit records are retained for a minimum of 6 years, with configuration to retain longer for states requiring a longer period.
requirements.quote: Retention 6 years minimum, configurable higher for states requiring longer

requirements.title: Audit records queryable by patient, user and date range
requirements.description: The system must allow audit records to be queried by patient, by user and by date range.
requirements.quote: Audit records queryable by patient, by user and by date range

requirements.title: Compliance officer produces tamper-evident PHI access record for an auditor
requirements.description: A compliance officer needs a complete and tamper-evident record of PHI access so that auditor questions can be answered without reconstructing data.
requirements.quote: As a compliance officer, I want a complete and tamper-evident record of PHI access so that I can answer an auditor without reconstructing anything.
requirements.trigger: An auditor requests evidence of PHI access
requirements.happyPath: The compliance officer queries the immutable audit log by patient, user or date range and exports a signed file for the auditor without reconstructing records.

requirements.title: Audit write is synchronous and blocks unlogged access
requirements.description: The audit write must occur synchronously with the access it records; if the access cannot be logged it must fail rather than proceed unlogged.
requirements.quote: Audit write is synchronous with the access it records — an access that cannot be logged must fail rather than proceed unlogged

requirements.title: Patient access history query under 3 seconds
requirements.description: A query for one patient's full access history must return in under 3 seconds.
requirements.quote: Query for one patient's full access history returns in under 3 seconds

requirements.title: No interface permits modification of an existing audit row
requirements.description: No API, admin console or database role may permit modification of an existing audit row.
requirements.quote: No API, admin console or database role permits modification of an existing audit row

requirements.title: Audit export produces signed file for auditor submission
requirements.description: Exporting audit data must produce a signed file suitable for submission to an auditor.
requirements.quote: Export produces a signed file suitable for submission to an auditor

requirements.title: Per-user behavioural baseline
requirements.description: The system must maintain a baseline per user covering records per day, departments touched, and hours of activity.
requirements.quote: Baseline per user: records per day, departments touched, hours of activity

requirements.title: Flag same-surname patient record access
requirements.description: Access to a record for a patient with the same surname as the accessing user must be flagged.
requirements.quote: Flag: access to a record for a patient with the same surname as the user

requirements.title: Flag VIP or employee record access
requirements.description: Access to a VIP or employee record must be flagged for review.
requirements.quote: Flag: access to a VIP or employee record

requirements.title: Flag volume more than three standard deviations above baseline
requirements.description: Access volume exceeding three standard deviations above the user's baseline must be flagged.
requirements.quote: Flag: volume more than three standard deviations above the user's baseline

requirements.title: Flag access outside the user's normal hours
requirements.description: Access outside the user's normal hours must be flagged, where the user has an established pattern.
requirements.quote: Flag: access outside the user's normal hours, where the user has an established pattern

requirements.title: Flag access without a recorded care relationship
requirements.description: A record accessed by a user with no care relationship recorded must be flagged.
requirements.quote: Flag: a record accessed by a user with no care relationship recorded

requirements.title: Privacy officer reviews surfaced unusual access
requirements.description: A privacy officer wants unusual access surfaced so that review effort focuses on what matters instead of reading every log line.
requirements.quote: As a privacy officer, I want unusual access surfaced so that I review what matters instead of reading every log line.
requirements.trigger: An anomalous PHI access is detected against the user baseline
requirements.happyPath: The system flags the anomalous access with reason and evidence within 30 minutes, the privacy officer reviews the flag, and the decision feeds back into the baseline.

requirements.title: Flags raised within 30 minutes of access
requirements.description: Anomaly flags must be raised within 30 minutes of the access that triggered them.
requirements.quote: Flags raised within 30 minutes of the access

requirements.title: False positive rate below 20% measured monthly
requirements.description: The anomaly detection false positive rate must remain below 20%, measured monthly against reviewer outcomes.
requirements.quote: False positive rate below 20%, measured monthly against reviewer outcomes

requirements.title: Flags include reason and triggering evidence
requirements.description: Each anomaly flag must carry the reason it was raised and the evidence that triggered it.
requirements.quote: Each flag carries the reason and the evidence that triggered it

requirements.title: Reviewer decisions feed back into the baseline
requirements.description: Decisions made by reviewers on flagged access must feed back into the user baseline used for anomaly detection.
requirements.quote: Reviewer decisions feed back into the baseline

requirements.title: Track right of access requests against statutory 30-day clock
requirements.description: A health information manager must be able to track patient right-of-access requests end to end against the statutory deadline so the 30-day limit is not missed. The journey covers intake, verification, assembly of the designated record set, and delivery.
requirements.quote: As a health information manager, I want to track access requests against the statutory clock so that we do not miss the 30-day deadline.
requirements.trigger: A patient submits a right of access request
requirements.happyPath: Request is received and logged, patient identity is verified, the designated record set is assembled excluding psychotherapy notes, and the records are delivered in the requested format within 30 days while days remaining are tracked throughout.

requirements.title: Capture access request intake details
requirements.description: At intake the system must record the patient's identity and the verification method used, the scope of records requested, the format requested, and the date the request was received.
requirements.quote: Request intake records: patient identity and verification method, scope requested, format requested, date received

requirements.title: Statutory clock starts on receipt
requirements.description: The 30-day response clock begins on the date the request is received, not on the date the patient's identity is verified.
requirements.quote: Clock starts on receipt, not on verification

requirements.title: One 30-day extension with prior written notice
requirements.description: A single 30-day extension of the access response deadline is permitted. It requires written notice to the patient delivered before day 30.
requirements.quote: One 30-day extension permitted, requiring written notice to the patient before day 30

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes excluded from designated record set assembly
requirements.description: When fulfilling an access request, the system assembles the designated record set and must exclude psychotherapy notes from the material provided.
requirements.quote: Fulfilment assembles the designated record set, excluding psychotherapy notes

requirements.title: Supported access request delivery methods
requirements.description: Fulfilled access requests must be deliverable by secure portal download, encrypted email, or physical media.
requirements.quote: Delivery methods: secure portal download, encrypted email, physical media

requirements.title: Days remaining shown on open requests
requirements.description: Every open access request displays the number of days remaining against the statutory deadline.
requirements.quote: Days remaining displayed on every open request

requirements.title: Extension blocked without proof of patient notification
requirements.description: The system must prevent an extension from being recorded unless there is evidence the patient was notified.
requirements.quote: Extension cannot be recorded without evidence the patient was notified

requirements.title: Escalate access requests approaching day 25
requirements.description: Access requests that approach day 25 of the statutory clock are escalated to the health information manager.
requirements.quote: Requests approaching day 25 escalate to the health information manager

requirements.title: Full audit trail across the access request lifecycle
requirements.description: An audit trail must capture the request, the verification, the assembly, the delivery, and the identity of every actor involved.
requirements.quote: Audit trail: request, verification, assembly, delivery, and the identity of every actor

requirements.title: Patient requests an accounting of disclosures
requirements.description: A patient must be able to request and receive a list of the parties their information was disclosed to, so they can see where it has gone.
requirements.quote: As a patient, I want a list of who my information was disclosed to, so that I can see where it has gone.
requirements.trigger: Patient submits a request for an accounting of disclosures
requirements.happyPath: The system compiles disclosures from the six years prior to the request, excludes treatment, payment and healthcare operations disclosures, and produces a patient-readable accounting within 60 days.

requirements.title: Accounting covers six years prior to the request
requirements.description: An accounting of disclosures must cover the six-year period immediately preceding the date of the patient's request.
requirements.quote: Accounting covers six years prior to the request

requirements.title: Treatment, payment and operations disclosures excluded from accounting
requirements.description: Disclosures made for treatment, payment and healthcare operations are excluded from the accounting of disclosures.
requirements.quote: Excludes treatment, payment and healthcare operations disclosures

requirements.title: Required content of each accounting entry
requirements.description: Each accounting entry must include the date of disclosure, the recipient's name and address, a description of the PHI disclosed, and the purpose of the disclosure.
requirements.quote: Includes: date, recipient name and address, description of PHI, and purpose

requirements.title: First accounting free per 12-month period; later requests may be charged
requirements.description: The first accounting of disclosures in any 12-month period is provided free of charge. Subsequent requests in the same period may carry a cost-based fee, provided notice of the fee is given.
requirements.quote: First accounting in any 12-month period is free; subsequent requests may carry a cost-based fee after notice

requirements.title: Accounting produced within 60 days of request
requirements.description: The accounting of disclosures must be generated and provided within 60 days of the patient's request.
requirements.quote: Accounting generated within 60 days of request

requirements.title: Exclusions verified by sampling
requirements.description: Excluded disclosure categories must be genuinely excluded from the accounting output, and this is verified by sampling.
requirements.quote: Excluded categories are genuinely excluded, verified by sampling

requirements.title: Accounting output is patient-readable
requirements.description: The accounting of disclosures must be presented in a form readable by a patient rather than as a raw system log.
requirements.quote: Output is readable by a patient, not a system log

requirements.title: Structured incident-to-breach-notification workflow for privacy officer
requirements.description: The system must provide a structured path taking a privacy officer from a suspected incident through to a notification decision, ensuring the four-factor assessment is always performed.
requirements.quote: As a privacy officer, I want a structured path from a suspected incident to a notification decision, so that the four-factor assessment is never skipped.
requirements.trigger: A suspected privacy incident is identified
requirements.happyPath: Incident is intaken, four-factor risk assessment is recorded, breach determination is made with reasoning, affected individuals are assembled, and notifications are issued from templates within the deadline.

requirements.title: Multi-channel incident intake
requirements.description: The system must support incident intake from anomaly flags, staff reports, patient complaints and vendor notifications.
requirements.quote: Incident intake from: anomaly flags, staff report, patient complaint, vendor notification

requirements.title: Explicit recording of four-factor risk assessment
requirements.description: The four-factor risk assessment must be recorded explicitly, covering the nature and extent of PHI, who received it, whether it was acquired or viewed, and mitigation.
requirements.quote: Four-factor risk assessment recorded explicitly: nature and extent of PHI, who received it, whether it was acquired or viewed, and mitigation

requirements.title: Presumption of breach unless low probability of compromise
requirements.description: An incident is presumed to be a breach unless the four-factor assessment concludes there is a low probability of compromise, and the reasoning for that conclusion must be recorded.
requirements.quote: Presumption of breach unless the assessment concludes low probability of compromise, with reasoning recorded

requirements.title: Affected individual list built from audit records
requirements.description: The system must assemble the list of affected individuals for a breach from audit records.
requirements.quote: Affected individual list assembled from audit records

requirements.title: Notification templates for individual, HHS and media
requirements.description: The system must provide breach notification templates for affected individuals, HHS and the media.
requirements.quote: Notification templates for individual, HHS and media

requirements.title: Non-reportable closure blocked without all four factors
requirements.description: The system must prevent a breach from being closed as non-reportable unless all four assessment factors have been recorded.
requirements.quote: A breach cannot be closed as non-reportable without all four factors recorded

requirements.title: 60-day notification countdown from discovery date
requirements.description: The system must display a countdown from the breach discovery date against a 60-day notification deadline.
requirements.quote: Countdown from discovery date displayed, 60-day deadline

requirements.title: Breaches of 500 or more individuals flagged for HHS timeline and media notice
requirements.description: Breaches affecting 500 or more individuals must be flagged for the separate HHS reporting timeline and for media notification.
requirements.quote: Breaches of 500 or more individuals flagged for the separate HHS timeline and media notice

requirements.title: Business associate notification dated from associate's discovery
requirements.description: Business associate notifications must be recorded using the date the associate discovered the incident, not the date the associate reported it to the covered entity.
requirements.quote: Business associate notifications recorded with the date the associate discovered the incident, not the date they told us

requirements.title: Record retrieval latency under 2 seconds at 95th percentile
requirements.description: The system must return patient record retrievals in under 2 seconds measured at the 95th percentile of requests.
requirements.quote: Record retrieval under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile

requirements.title: Break-glass access grant under 5 seconds
requirements.description: When emergency break-glass access is invoked, the system must complete the access grant in under 5 seconds.
requirements.quote: Break-glass grant under 5 seconds

requirements.title: Single-patient audit query under 3 seconds
requirements.description: An audit query scoped to one patient must return results in under 3 seconds.
requirements.quote: Audit query for one patient under 3 seconds

requirements.title: Support minimum 200 concurrent clinical users
requirements.description: The system must support at least 200 concurrent clinical users while meeting stated performance targets.
requirements.quote: 200 concurrent clinical users minimum

requirements.title: AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit
requirements.description: Data must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 and encrypted in transit using TLS version 1.2 or higher.
requirements.quote: Encryption at rest AES-256, in transit TLS 1.2 or higher

requirements.title: Unique user identification with no shared accounts
requirements.description: Every user must have a unique identifier; shared accounts are prohibited and the prohibition must be enforced technically by the system rather than by policy alone.
requirements.quote: Unique user identification; no shared accounts, enforced by the system

requirements.title: Automatic logoff after 15 minutes of inactivity
requirements.description: Clinical workstations must automatically log the user off after 15 minutes of inactivity.
requirements.quote: Automatic logoff after 15 minutes of inactivity on clinical workstations

requirements.title: Key management separated from data storage with documented rotation
requirements.description: Encryption key management must be kept separate from the data storage environment, and key rotation procedures must be documented.
requirements.quote: Key management separated from data storage with documented rotation

requirements.title: Multi-factor authentication for remote access
requirements.description: All remote access to the system must require multi-factor authentication.
requirements.quote: Multi-factor authentication for remote access

requirements.title: 99.9% platform uptime
requirements.description: The platform must maintain 99.9% uptime; clinical systems must remain available during care delivery.
requirements.quote: 99.9% uptime; clinical systems cannot be unavailable during care

requirements.title: Recovery time objective of 4 hours
requirements.description: Following a disruption, the platform must be restored within a recovery time objective of 4 hours.
requirements.quote: Recovery time objective 4 hours, recovery point objective 15 minutes

requirements.title: Recovery point objective of 15 minutes
requirements.description: Data loss in a recovery scenario must not exceed 15 minutes, per the stated recovery point objective.
requirements.quote: Recovery time objective 4 hours, recovery point objective 15 minutes

requirements.title: Documented emergency mode operation
requirements.description: Emergency mode operating procedures must be documented for use when the platform is unavailable, so care can continue.
requirements.quote: Documented emergency mode operation when the platform is unavailable

requirements.title: Minimum necessary enforced at record-section level
requirements.description: The platform must enforce the minimum necessary principle with granularity down to individual record sections.
requirements.quote: Minimum necessary enforced at record-section level

requirements.title: Safe Harbor de-identification for research extracts
requirements.description: The platform must provide de-identification of data for research extracts using the Safe Harbor method.
requirements.quote: De-identification available for research extracts, using the Safe Harbor method

requirements.title: GDPR erasure requests for EU patients
requirements.description: Erasure requests from EU patients must be honoured, except where a legal retention obligation applies.
requirements.quote: GDPR: erasure requests honoured for EU patients where no legal retention obligation applies

requirements.title: Patient-to-patient messaging excluded from MVP
requirements.description: Direct messaging between patients is explicitly out of scope for the MVP release; the system will not provide patient-to-patient message channels in this version.
requirements.quote: Direct patient-to-patient messaging

requirements.title: Genomic data storage excluded from MVP
requirements.description: The MVP will not store genomic data. No genomic data types are to be persisted by the system in this release.
requirements.quote: Genomic data storage

requirements.title: Clinical decision support excluded from MVP
requirements.description: Clinical decision support functionality is out of scope for the MVP and will not be delivered in this release.
requirements.quote: Clinical decision support

requirements.title: Automated expert-determination de-identification excluded from MVP
requirements.description: Automated de-identification using the expert determination method is out of scope for the MVP; only other de-identification approaches (if any) are in scope for this release.
requirements.quote: Automated de-identification using expert determination

requirements.title: Governing state retention period for multi-state treatment must be resolved
requirements.description: An open decision remains on which state's retention period applies when a patient has received treatment in more than one state; the retention rule must be determined before retention logic is finalized.
requirements.quote: Which state retention period governs when a patient has been treated in more than one state?

requirements.title: Break-glass patient notification trigger to be decided
requirements.description: It must be decided whether break-glass access notifies the patient automatically or only upon privacy officer confirmation, before notification behavior is implemented.
requirements.quote: Should break-glass notify the patient automatically, or on privacy officer confirmation?

requirements.title: De-identification method scope decision (Safe Harbor vs expert determination)
requirements.description: A decision is required on whether the system supports the expert determination method for de-identification or Safe Harbor only.
requirements.quote: Do we support the expert determination method for de-identification, or Safe Harbor only?

requirements.title: Approved verification method for telephone right-of-access requests undefined
requirements.description: The approved method for verifying the identity of a requester who submits a right-of-access request by telephone has not yet been determined and must be defined.
requirements.quote: What is the approved verification method for a right-of-access request received by telephone?

requirements.title: Support multi-facility, multi-state network scale
requirements.description: The platform must support an organization operating 4 hospitals and 31 outpatient clinics across three states, serving approximately 480,000 patients annually.
requirements.quote: Meridian Regional Health operates 4 hospitals and 31 outpatient clinics across three states, serving roughly 480,000 patients a year.

requirements.title: Answer auditor questions without manual reconstruction
requirements.description: The replacement records platform must be able to respond to an auditor's questions directly, eliminating the manual reconstruction process that currently takes days.
requirements.quote: It is replacing a records platform that cannot answer an auditor's questions without a manual reconstruction taking days.

requirements.title: Privacy team reviews only anomalous access
requirements.description: Rather than reading access logs line by line, the privacy team should only need to review access events flagged as anomalous. Access log review must be driven by anomaly detection.
requirements.quote: The target is that they read only what is anomalous

requirements.title: Right-of-access requests fulfilled in days
requirements.description: Patient right-of-access requests must be fulfilled within days, improving on the current average fulfilment time of 26 days.
requirements.quote: a right-of-access request is fulfilled in days rather than the current average of 26

requirements.title: Dual HIPAA status as covered entity and business associate
requirements.description: MRH operates both as a covered entity under HIPAA and as a business associate for two payer partners, so the compliance programme must satisfy obligations arising from both roles simultaneously.
requirements.quote: Covered entity under HIPAA; also a business associate for two payer partners

requirements.title: HIPAA Privacy, Security and HITECH breach notification apply
requirements.description: The regulatory environment includes the HIPAA Privacy Rule, the HIPAA Security Rule and HITECH breach notification obligations, which govern the handling of PHI and the reporting of breaches.
requirements.quote: HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules, HITECH breach notification

requirements.title: 42 CFR Part 2 obligations for behavioural health service line
requirements.description: The behavioural health service line brings substance use disorder confidentiality obligations under 42 CFR Part 2 into scope, in addition to HIPAA.
requirements.quote: Behavioural health service line, bringing 42 CFR Part 2 obligations

requirements.title: GDPR in scope for EU patients at one facility
requirements.description: EU patients treated at one facility near an international airport bring GDPR into scope for a small population, requiring GDPR-compliant handling for those records.
requirements.quote: EU patients treated at one facility near an international airport, bringing GDPR into scope for a small population

requirements.title: Seven-year retention statute in one state
requirements.description: One of the three states in which MRH operates imposes a records retention period of 7 years.
requirements.quote: Three state retention statutes: 7 years, 10 years, and 10 years past the age of majority for minors

requirements.title: Ten-year retention statute in one state
requirements.description: One of the three states in which MRH operates imposes a records retention period of 10 years.
requirements.quote: Three state retention statutes: 7 years, 10 years, and 10 years past the age of majority for minors

requirements.title: Minor records retained 10 years past age of majority
requirements.description: One state retention statute requires records for minors to be retained for 10 years past the age of majority, meaning retention clocks for minors must be computed from date of birth rather than date of service.
requirements.quote: Three state retention statutes: 7 years, 10 years, and 10 years past the age of majority for minors

requirements.title: Retention rules vary by state across the care network
requirements.description: MRH operates 4 hospitals and 31 clinics across 3 states, each with its own retention statute, so retention handling must be applied per state rather than uniformly.
requirements.quote: 4 hospitals, 31 clinics, 3 states (each with its own retention statute)

requirements.title: Roughly 6,200 of 11,000 staff touch PHI
requirements.description: Of approximately 11,000 staff, roughly 6,200 handle PHI, defining the population subject to access controls, training and monitoring.
requirements.quote: 11,000 staff, of whom roughly 6,200 touch PHI

requirements.title: Privacy team staffing constraint
requirements.description: The privacy function consists of 4 analysts and 1 privacy officer, which bounds the volume of manual review, monitoring and investigation work the programme can absorb.
requirements.quote: Privacy team: 4 analysts and 1 privacy officer

requirements.title: Joint Commission accreditation survey scheduled for 2026
requirements.description: A Joint Commission accreditation survey is scheduled for 2026, requiring the organisation's compliance evidence and documentation to be survey-ready by that date.
requirements.quote: Joint Commission accreditation survey scheduled for 2026

requirements.title: Annual security attestation required by two payer contracts
requirements.description: Two payer contracts require MRH to produce an annual security attestation, creating a recurring contractual reporting obligation.
requirements.quote: Two payer contracts requiring annual security attestation

requirements.title: Same-day clinical role provisioning on hire
requirements.description: Attending clinicians must have their clinical access role provisioned on the same day they are hired, following completion of credentialing.
requirements.quote: Expected provisioning time: same day on hire

requirements.title: Credentialing completion triggers identity provisioning
requirements.description: The identity team provisions the clinical role only after credentialing for the clinician has completed.
requirements.quote: Credentialing completes and the identity team provisions the clinical role

requirements.title: Multi-factor authentication for clinician login
requirements.description: Attending clinicians must authenticate with multi-factor authentication before accessing PHI.
requirements.quote: Clinician logs in with multi-factor authentication

requirements.title: Panel records accessible without additional approval
requirements.description: Records for patients within the clinician's own panel (patients in their care) are available with full clinical record access and require no further approval step.
requirements.quote: Records for their panel are available without further approval

requirements.title: Break-glass with stated reason for out-of-panel records
requirements.description: Access to a record outside the clinician's panel is only permitted through the break-glass path, and the clinician must state a reason for the access.
requirements.quote: A record outside the panel requires break-glass with a stated reason
requirements.trigger: Attempt to open a record outside the clinician's panel

requirements.title: Privacy officer review of break-glass events within 5 business days
requirements.description: Every break-glass event raised by an attending clinician must be reviewed by the privacy officer within 5 business days of the event.
requirements.quote: Privacy officer reviews the break-glass event within 5 business days

requirements.title: Access from shared workstations and personal mobile devices
requirements.description: The system must support attending clinician access from shared clinical workstations and personal mobile devices, which are identified as risk factors alongside high access volume.
requirements.quote: Risk factors: shared workstations, mobile access, high volume

requirements.title: Attending clinician access journey from credentialing to break-glass review
requirements.description: End-to-end journey for an attending clinician: credentialing completes and the clinical role is provisioned, the clinician authenticates with MFA, accesses panel records freely, uses break-glass with a stated reason for out-of-panel records, and the privacy officer reviews that event.
requirements.quote: 1. Credentialing completes and the identity team provisions the clinical role
requirements.trigger: Clinician is hired and credentialing completes
requirements.happyPath: Identity team provisions the clinical role, clinician logs in with MFA, opens panel records without further approval, invokes break-glass with a stated reason when a record falls outside the panel, and the privacy officer reviews the break-glass event within 5 business days.

requirements.title: Attending clinician access volume profile
requirements.description: Attending clinicians represent 48% of PHI-touching staff and access 20-60 records per shift, mostly within their own panel; this volume profile shapes monitoring and provisioning expectations.
requirements.quote: Access pattern: 20-60 records per shift, mostly their own panel

requirements.title: Expected break-glass frequency for clinicians
requirements.description: Break-glass access is expected to be needed a few times a month per the attending clinician persona, typically in the emergency department, and is treated as the exception path rather than routine access.
requirements.quote: Break-glass needed a few times a month, typically in the emergency department

requirements.title: Part 2 consent required for disclosures beyond general HIPAA consent
requirements.description: For behavioural health records, 42 CFR Part 2 applies, requiring a specific consent for disclosures that a general HIPAA consent would otherwise permit.
requirements.quote: 42 CFR Part 2 applies: consent required for disclosures a general HIPAA consent would permit

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes need separate authorisation and are excluded from right of access
requirements.description: Psychotherapy notes require a separate authorisation to be disclosed and are not included in the patient's right of access.
requirements.quote: Psychotherapy notes require separate authorisation and are excluded from the right of access

requirements.title: Substance use records must be segregable
requirements.description: The system must keep substance use disorder treatment records segregable so they can be withheld from a general disclosure.
requirements.quote: Substance use records must be segregable so they can be withheld from a general disclosure

requirements.title: Same-day provisioning with a second approval for behavioural health clinicians
requirements.description: Access provisioning for behavioural health clinicians is expected to complete the same day, but requires a second approval step.
requirements.quote: Expected provisioning time: same day, but with a second approval

requirements.title: Every Part 2 record access reviewed individually
requirements.description: All accesses to 42 CFR Part 2 records are reviewed in full rather than through sampling.
requirements.quote: Monitoring: every access to a Part 2 record is reviewed, not sampled

requirements.title: Behavioural health role provisioning requires two approvers
requirements.description: The behavioural health scope role must be provisioned through a workflow that requires two approvers.
requirements.quote: Role provisioned with behavioural health scope, requiring two approvers

requirements.title: Part 2 records visible only with patient-specific consent
requirements.description: The system must make Part 2 records visible to the clinician only where a Part 2 consent exists for that specific patient.
requirements.quote: Part 2 records visible only where a Part 2 consent exists for that patient

requirements.title: Disclosure requests checked against consent before release
requirements.description: Every disclosure request involving behavioural health records must be validated against the recorded consent prior to any release.
requirements.quote: Any disclosure request checked against consent before release

requirements.title: Redisclosure prohibition attached to outgoing Part 2 records
requirements.description: A redisclosure prohibition notice must be attached to every Part 2 record that leaves the system.
requirements.quote: Redisclosure prohibition attached to every Part 2 record leaving the system

requirements.title: Behavioural health clinician access journey
requirements.description: A behavioural health clinician (psychiatrist, psychologist or licensed counsellor) is provisioned with behavioural health scope and works with a small number of highly sensitive records including psychotherapy notes and substance use disorder treatment.
