requirements.quote: Psychiatrists, psychologists, licensed counsellors
requirements.trigger: Clinician requires access to behavioural health records for treatment
requirements.happyPath: Role provisioned with behavioural health scope after two approvals on the same day; clinician sees Part 2 records only where patient consent exists; disclosure requests are checked against consent and released with a redisclosure prohibition; each access is individually reviewed.

requirements.title: Revenue Cycle Analyst access limited to codes and demographics
requirements.description: The Revenue Cycle Analyst role must be scoped under the minimum necessary principle to diagnosis and procedure codes plus demographics, with no access to clinical narrative or notes.
requirements.quote: Minimum necessary is the governing principle: codes and demographics, no notes

requirements.title: Two business day provisioning for billing role
requirements.description: Access provisioning for the Revenue Cycle Analyst role is expected to complete within 2 business days.
requirements.quote: Expected provisioning time: 2 business days

requirements.title: Baseline access volume monitoring per analyst
requirements.description: The system must establish a baseline record access volume for each Revenue Cycle Analyst and flag deviations from that baseline.
requirements.quote: Monitoring: baseline volume per analyst, flag on deviation

requirements.title: Provision analyst role with billing scope
requirements.description: Revenue Cycle Analysts are provisioned with a role carrying billing scope only.
requirements.quote: Role provisioned with billing scope

requirements.title: Records opened from the claims queue rather than search
requirements.description: Analysts access patient records only by opening them from an assigned claims queue; record access is not initiated via search.
requirements.quote: Analyst works a claims queue; records open from the queue, not by search

requirements.title: Free-text patient name search disabled for billing role
requirements.description: The system must disable free-text search of patient names for the Revenue Cycle Analyst role.
requirements.quote: Free-text search of patient names is disabled for this role

requirements.title: Out-of-baseline volume flagged for review
requirements.description: Access volume that falls outside an analyst's established baseline is flagged for review.
requirements.quote: Volume outside the baseline is flagged for review

requirements.title: Revenue Cycle Analyst claims processing journey
requirements.description: A Revenue Cycle Analyst is provisioned with billing scope, works records from an assigned claims queue without search capability, and has access volume monitored against a baseline with deviations flagged.
requirements.quote: Billing, coding and claims staff
requirements.trigger: Analyst is assigned a claims queue after role provisioning
requirements.happyPath: Role is provisioned with billing scope; the analyst opens records from the claims queue; access is limited to codes and demographics; volume stays within baseline and no review is triggered.

requirements.title: Research partners have no direct system access
requirements.description: External research partners must not be granted interactive access to the system; data is provided only as generated extracts.
requirements.quote: No direct system access; extracts only

requirements.title: Research access pattern is bulk extract
requirements.description: Access for academic researchers under a data use agreement is delivered as a bulk extract rather than interactive querying.
requirements.quote: Access pattern: bulk extract, not interactive

requirements.title: Data use agreement required before limited data set release
requirements.description: A limited data set may only be released after a data use agreement has been executed with the receiving institution.
requirements.quote: Limited data set requires a data use agreement before release

requirements.title: Safe Harbor de-identification removes 18 identifier types
requirements.description: Fully de-identified research extracts must be produced by the Safe Harbor method, with all 18 identifier types removed.
requirements.quote: De-identification by Safe Harbor: 18 identifier types removed

requirements.title: IRB approval recorded before any extract
requirements.description: IRB approval must be obtained and recorded in the system before any research extract is generated or released.
requirements.quote: IRB approval required and recorded before any extract

requirements.title: Research extract turnaround of 2-4 weeks
requirements.description: The expected turnaround time from research request to released extract is 2-4 weeks.
requirements.quote: Expected turnaround: 2-4 weeks

requirements.title: Every research extract logged with institution and IRB
requirements.description: The system must log every research extract, capturing the requesting institution and the approving IRB.
requirements.quote: Monitoring: every extract logged with the requesting institution and the approving IRB

requirements.title: Privacy officer determines extract type
requirements.description: The privacy officer must decide whether a limited data set or a fully de-identified extract is appropriate for each research request.
requirements.quote: Privacy officer determines whether a limited data set or de-identified extract is appropriate

requirements.title: Extract released through secure transfer
requirements.description: Research extracts must be generated, reviewed and released via secure transfer.
requirements.quote: Extract generated, reviewed and released through secure transfer

requirements.title: Research extract recorded in accounting of disclosures
requirements.description: Each released research extract must be recorded in the accounting of disclosures.
requirements.quote: Extract recorded in the accounting of disclosures

requirements.title: Annual attestation from receiving institution
requirements.description: The receiving institution must provide an annual attestation that the data has been handled in accordance with the data use agreement.
requirements.quote: Annual attestation from the institution that data has been handled per agreement

requirements.title: External research partner obtains a data extract
requirements.description: An academic researcher under a data use agreement requests data; the request is assessed, agreements executed, and an extract released and recorded.
requirements.quote: Academic researchers under a data use agreement
requirements.trigger: Research request received with IRB approval documentation
requirements.happyPath: Research request received with IRB approval documentation; privacy officer determines whether a limited data set or de-identified extract is appropriate; data use agreement executed if a limited data set; extract generated, reviewed and released through secure transfer; extract recorded in the accounting of disclosures; annual attestation received from the institution.

requirements.title: Retention period determined by strictest applicable state rule
requirements.description: Where multiple state retention rules apply to a record, the platform must apply the longest/strictest applicable retention period on a per-record basis, so that a patient treated in two states inherits the longer period.
requirements.quote: Retention determined per record by the strictest applicable rule

requirements.title: Cross-state patient inherits longer retention period
requirements.description: A patient who has been treated in two states is subject to the longer of the two applicable retention periods.
requirements.quote: A patient treated in two states inherits the longer period

requirements.title: Minor records retained until 10 years past age of majority
requirements.description: In one of MRH's states, records for minors must be retained until 10 years past the age of majority, which can amount to a retention period of up to 28 years.
requirements.quote: Minors in one state must be retained until 10 years past the age of majority, which can be 28 years

requirements.title: Early deletion is a statutory violation; over-retention increases breach exposure
requirements.description: Deleting records before the applicable retention period expires constitutes a statutory violation, while retaining everything indefinitely increases breach exposure — retention must therefore be bounded on both ends.
requirements.quote: Deleting too early is a statutory violation; keeping everything forever raises breach exposure

requirements.title: Retention clock displayed on the record
requirements.description: The platform must display the retention clock on each record so users can see the applicable retention period and remaining time.
requirements.quote: Retention clock visible on the record

requirements.title: No bulk deletion path bypassing per-record retention rules
requirements.description: The system must not provide any bulk deletion capability that can circumvent the per-record retention rule evaluation.
requirements.quote: No bulk deletion path that can bypass the per-record rule

requirements.title: Disposal certificates retained after destruction
requirements.description: After a record is destroyed, the corresponding disposal certificate must be retained as evidence of compliant destruction.
requirements.quote: Disposal certificates retained after destruction

requirements.title: Single platform supports three differing state retention regimes
requirements.description: The platform must reconcile three different state retention rule sets across three states within one system.
requirements.quote: Three states, three retention rules, one platform.

requirements.title: Risk-based triage of break-glass events
requirements.description: Break-glass access events must be triaged and prioritized by risk score rather than presented to reviewers as an undifferentiated flat list, so that a single privacy officer can handle the volume generated by 6,200 staff.
requirements.quote: Break-glass events triaged by risk, not presented as a flat list

requirements.title: Mandatory individual review for high-sensitivity access categories
requirements.description: Break-glass events involving same-surname matches, VIP records, or employee records must always be routed for individual review and can never be batch-reviewed.
requirements.quote: Same-surname, VIP and employee-record access always reviewed individually

requirements.title: Batch review permitted for ED break-glass during documented trauma activation
requirements.description: Break-glass events originating in the emergency department during a documented trauma activation are eligible for batch review rather than individual review.
requirements.quote: Emergency department break-glass during a documented trauma activation may be reviewed in batch

requirements.title: Every break-glass event has a recorded decision
requirements.description: Regardless of whether an event is reviewed individually or in batch, a review decision must be recorded for every break-glass event.
requirements.quote: Every event has a decision recorded, whatever the review path

requirements.title: Break-glass review must be demonstrable in a survey
requirements.description: The organization cannot leave break-glass events unreviewed, as an absence of review is not defensible during a regulatory survey; the review process and its outcomes must be evidenced.
requirements.quote: Reviewing nothing is not defensible in a survey

requirements.title: Missed inappropriate access escalates to a reportable breach
requirements.description: A single inappropriate access that is missed during break-glass review can become a reportable breach, so triage must minimize the risk of unreviewed high-risk events.
requirements.quote: A single missed inappropriate access can become a reportable breach

requirements.title: Break-glass review volume must scale to 6,200 staff
requirements.description: The break-glass review solution must handle the event volume generated by 6,200 staff within the capacity of the existing privacy team, since reviewing every event manually is not achievable.
requirements.quote: Reviewing everything is not achievable with the current team

requirements.title: Dual role as business associate and covered entity
requirements.description: The system must account for MRH acting as a business associate for two payers in addition to its role as a covered entity, applying business associate obligations alongside covered entity obligations.
requirements.quote: MRH is a business associate for two payers, not only a covered entity.

requirements.title: Incident reporting to payers within contractual window
requirements.description: Security and privacy incidents affecting payer data must be reported to the affected payer within the window defined in the business associate contract, which is shorter than HIPAA's 60-day notification period. The system must track and enforce the shorter contractual deadline rather than defaulting to 60 days.
requirements.quote: Incident reporting to the payer within their contractual window, which is shorter than HIPAA's 60 days

requirements.title: Automated annual security attestation from system evidence
requirements.description: The system must generate the annual security attestation required by payers directly from system-held evidence, rather than requiring manual assembly of the attestation package.
requirements.quote: Annual security attestation produced from system evidence, not assembled by hand

requirements.title: Documented subcontractor flow-down for payer data vendors
requirements.description: Subcontractor flow-down of business associate obligations must be documented for every vendor that touches payer data, with no exceptions.
requirements.quote: Subcontractor flow-down documented for every vendor touching payer data

requirements.title: System must scale to 4.2 million patient records
requirements.description: The privacy and PHI access platform must support an operational corpus of 4.2 million patient records.
requirements.quote: Patient records: 4.2 million

requirements.title: PHI access event volume of 180,000-240,000 per day
requirements.description: The monitoring and audit capability must ingest and process between 180,000 and 240,000 PHI access events each day.
requirements.quote: PHI access events: 180,000-240,000 per day

requirements.title: Break-glass event volume of 300-500 per month
requirements.description: The system must handle a break-glass emergency access volume of 300 to 500 events per month, which sets the sizing for break-glass review workload.
requirements.quote: Break-glass events: 300-500 per month

requirements.title: Right-of-access request volume of 220-400 per month
requirements.description: The patient rights workflow must process between 220 and 400 right-of-access requests per month.
requirements.quote: Right-of-access requests: 220-400 per month

requirements.title: Amendment request volume of 15-30 per month
requirements.description: The patient rights workflow must process between 15 and 30 record amendment requests per month.
requirements.quote: Amendment requests: 15-30 per month

requirements.title: Accounting of disclosures request volume of 5-15 per month
requirements.description: The disclosure accounting capability must handle between 5 and 15 accounting of disclosures requests per month.
requirements.quote: Accounting of disclosures requests: 5-15 per month

requirements.title: Research extract volume of 8-12 per quarter
requirements.description: The research data provisioning process must support 8 to 12 research extracts per quarter.
requirements.quote: Research extracts: 8-12 per quarter

requirements.title: Privacy team staffing constraint of 5 people
requirements.description: All privacy review workload must be handled by a privacy team of five staff, constraining the volume of manual review that can be performed.
requirements.quote: **Operational constraint:** privacy team of 5.

requirements.title: Automated prioritisation of review workload
requirements.description: Given the volume of access events relative to a five-person privacy team, the system must automate review so that only material events are surfaced for human attention.
requirements.quote: Automation is the only path to reviewing what matters.

requirements.title: Right-of-access fulfilment averaging under 10 days
requirements.description: Average turnaround for patient right-of-access requests must fall to under 10 days, improved from a baseline of 26 days.
requirements.quote: Right-of-access fulfilment under 10 days average, from 26

requirements.title: 70% reduction in privacy analyst log review time
requirements.description: Time spent by privacy analysts reviewing access logs must be reduced by 70% relative to the current baseline.
requirements.quote: Privacy analyst time on log review reduced by 70%

requirements.title: Break-glass review within 5 business days for all events
requirements.description: Every break-glass access event must have its review completed within 5 business days, with no exceptions (100% of events).
requirements.quote: Break-glass review completed within 5 business days for 100% of events

requirements.title: No Part 2 record access without recorded consent
requirements.description: There must be zero instances of access to 42 CFR Part 2 substance use disorder records where no consent is recorded.
requirements.quote: Zero access to Part 2 records without a recorded consent

requirements.title: Complete audit log capture of PHI access
requirements.description: 100% of PHI access events must be captured in the audit log.
requirements.quote: 100% of PHI access captured in the audit log

requirements.title: Breach risk assessments documented against all four factors
requirements.description: Every breach risk assessment must be documented against all four required factors, without exception.
requirements.quote: Breach risk assessments documented against all four factors, without exception

requirements.title: Retention applied per record by strictest applicable state rule
requirements.description: Retention periods must be applied on a per-record basis using the strictest applicable state rule.
requirements.quote: Retention applied per record by the strictest applicable state rule

requirements.title: Audit evidence producible within 2 business days for a survey
requirements.description: The system must be able to produce audit evidence for a regulatory survey within 2 business days.
requirements.quote: Audit evidence producible for a survey within 2 business days

requirements.title: 99.9% uptime
requirements.description: The system must maintain 99.9% uptime.
requirements.quote: Uptime 99.9%

requirements.title: Record retrieval under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile
requirements.description: Record retrieval response time must be under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile.
requirements.quote: Record retrieval under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile

requirements.title: Support 200 concurrent clinical users
requirements.description: The system must support 200 concurrent clinical users.
requirements.quote: 200 concurrent clinical users supported

requirements.title: Decide break-glass patient notification trigger
requirements.description: An open decision is required on whether break-glass access automatically notifies the affected patient, or whether notification only occurs after the privacy officer confirms the access was inappropriate. The notification design cannot be finalised until this is resolved.
requirements.quote: Should break-glass notify the patient automatically, or only after the privacy officer confirms the access was inappropriate?

requirements.title: Assign ownership of cross-state retention decisions
requirements.description: An open decision is required on who owns the retention decision when a patient is treated across state lines: the treating facility or a central function. Retention governance cannot be applied consistently until ownership is assigned.
requirements.quote: Who owns the retention decision when a patient is treated across state lines — the treating facility or a central function?

requirements.title: Decide whether batch review is acceptable for ED break-glass during trauma activations
requirements.description: An open decision is required on whether batch review of emergency department break-glass access is acceptable during documented trauma activations, and what evidence would support that position.
requirements.quote: Do we accept batch review for emergency department break-glass during documented trauma activations, and what evidence supports that?

requirements.title: Define verification standard for telephone right-of-access requests
requirements.description: An open decision is required on the identity verification standard applied when a right-of-access request arrives by telephone rather than through the patient portal.
requirements.quote: What is the verification standard for a right-of-access request arriving by telephone rather than through the portal?

requirements.title: Decide workflow routing for EU patient erasure requests
requirements.description: An open decision is required on whether erasure requests from EU patients are handled through the same workflow as record amendment requests, or through a separate dedicated workflow.
requirements.quote: Should EU patient erasure requests be handled by the same workflow as amendment requests, or separately?
